spec: DESIGN.md — installations, the machine seam, standalone save cards (issue #181)
description: Whole fixture machines in; the canonical SavefilePlacement serialization (atlas/contract.py) out, asserted with exact equality — for catalogue entries whose launch command names a standalone emulator a packaged save card covers. The card is the thin cited half (atlas/data/standalone_saves.json); the resolver reads the emulator's own configuration the way the emulator does, at the revision the arrangement ships (Dolphin 2603a). Root kind is emulator_directory: no frontend hands these emulators a save root.

vectors.name: dolphin-keeps-one-gci-folder-per-region-and-the-region-is-a-hole
vectors.rationale: The GCI-folder device sits in slot A (Dolphin.ini [Core] SlotA = 8, the registered default), so a GameCube save is one .gci file in <GC user>/<region>/Card A — named from the save's own directory entry, which no read of the content path recovers. The answer's dir keeps the <region> segment as a hole a caller with metadata fills, while the groups list all three region trees so a caller without it still sees the whole candidate set. RetroDECK reroutes the region trees with symlinks; the emulator-view dirs are the answer's.

vectors.name: xemus-saves-live-inside-the-emulated-hard-disk
vectors.rationale: Every Xbox save lives on the emulated hard disk — a disk image xemu.toml names, which the arrangement keeps beside the firmware. The image is one shared file; per-title structure exists only inside its FATX filesystem, so the save-inside-image caveat states the layout machine-readably (UDATA/<title id>) for a tool that can parse it, and a file-level client backs the image up whole. The EEPROM rides as its own named settings group. The configuration is read where xemu opens it — under the data home — which on this arrangement is a link back to a directory in the config tree, the shape RetroDECK builds on purpose ('linking back to original location where component will look', component_prepare.sh:16-17). The answer walks the link and names the location the emulator opens, not the one the distribution finds tidy.

vectors.name: duckstation-both-slots-hold-a-card-and-the-answer-names-both
vectors.rationale: A second controller port gets a second card, and the console's two slots then lie side by side in one directory. The answer's flat file list is every name in the directory it points at, in slot order — the FileSet invariant — so slot 2's card is in it and in its own group, whatever type each slot holds. Naming only slot 1 was not a smaller answer but no answer at all: it contradicted the invariant, and the question raised instead of answering. The headline stays slot 1's: dir and granularity.value come from the first group, while granularity.mode names the pair.

vectors.name: retrodeck-duckstations-dataroot-is-the-config-side-its-sandbox-pins
vectors.rationale: Nothing on this machine holds a DuckStation settings.ini, and that used to leave the DataRoot an open question: the emulator picks it from whether XDG_CONFIG_HOME is set (qthost.cpp:562-582), so the answer named the environment-unset side — the data one — and said the environment decides. It does not decide here. Every emulator RetroDECK ships runs inside RetroDECK's own flatpak, and flatpak force-pins XDG_CONFIG_HOME to the per-app config directory after applying every override (flatpak-context.c:3158-3187 at 1.16.6), so the set branch is the only branch such a launch can take. The compiled defaults now hang off the config side, where this launch really composes them: slot pair PerGameTitle/None (settings.h:510-511), memcards below that DataRoot — and no degradation, because nothing is degraded.
